title: CBSE Class 12 Computer Science · Practice paper 2
subject: Computer Science
label: Practice paper
instr: All questions are compulsory. However, internal choices have been provided in some questions. Attempt only one of the choices in such questions.
The paper is divided into 5 Sections: A, B, C, D and E.
Section A consists of 21 questions (1 to 21). Each question carries 1 mark.
Section B consists of 7 questions (22 to 28). Each question carries 2 marks.
Section C consists of 3 questions (29 to 31). Each question carries 3 marks.
Section D consists of 4 questions (32 to 35). Each question carries 4 marks.
Section E consists of 2 questions (36 and 37). Each question carries 5 marks.
All programming questions are to be answered using Python Language only.
In case of MCQ, text of the correct answer should also be written.

questions.text: Which condition, used in the WHERE clause, selects the names that have 'a' as the second letter (such as 'Rajat' and 'Kavya')?

questions.subject: Computer Science
questions.text: A. What is the difference between a function that returns a value and a function that does not return a value? What does a function return if it has no return statement? Explain with an example.
questions.model:
A function that returns a value uses a return statement to send a result back to the place where it was called; the result can be stored or used in an expression. A function that does not return a value only does its task (for example, prints something). Such a function returns None by default.
def area(l, b):
    return l * b          # returns a value

def show_area(l, b):
    print(l * b)          # returns nothing

x = area(4, 5)            # x is 20
y = show_area(4, 5)       # prints 20, y is None

points.t: Correct difference between the two kinds of function
Returns None by default
Suitable example

or.text: B. What is the use of the global keyword in a Python function? Explain with an example.
or.model:
A variable that is assigned inside a function is local to that function. The global keyword tells Python that the name refers to the global variable, so the function can change the value of the global variable.
count = 0
def increase():
    global count
    count = count + 1

increase()
increase()
print(count)              # 2

points.t: Correct use: lets a function change (assign to) a global variable
Suitable example using global

A. Write a Python function vowel_words(sentence) that takes a string and returns a list of the words in it that begin with a vowel (upper or lower case).
Example: vowel_words("An apple a day keeps illness away") should return ['An', 'apple', 'a', 'illness', 'away'].

def vowel_words(sentence):
    result = []
    for w in sentence.split():
        if w[0] in "aeiouAEIOU":
            result.append(w)
    return result

points.t: Correct function header
Correct logic: split into words and check the first letter against the vowels
Correct return of the list

or.text:
B. Write a Python function freq(L) that takes a list L and returns a dictionary in which each element of L is a key and its value is the number of times the element occurs in L.
Example: freq([3, 1, 3, 2, 1, 3]) should return {3: 3, 1: 2, 2: 1}.
or.model:
def freq(L):
    d = {}
    for x in L:
        if x in d:
            d[x] = d[x] + 1
        else:
            d[x] = 1
    return d

points.t: Correct function header
Correct logic for counting with a dictionary
Correct return of the dictionary

questions.subject: Computer Science
questions.text: A. Differentiate between bandwidth and data transfer rate. Write the unit in which each is measured.
questions.model:
Bandwidth is the range of frequencies available for the transmission of data through a channel; it is the capacity of the channel. It is measured in Hertz (Hz).
Data transfer rate is the number of bits sent from the sender to the receiver per second. It is measured in bits per second (bps), with larger units such as Kbps, Mbps and Gbps.

points.t: Correct meaning of bandwidth with its unit Hertz (Hz)
Correct meaning of data transfer rate with its unit bits per second (bps)

or.text: B. What is an IP address? Why does every device on the Internet need one? Give an example of an IPv4 address.
or.model: An IP address is a unique numeric address given to each device (node) connected to a network. It identifies the device, so that data can be sent to the right device on the Internet. Example: 192.168.1.10

points.t: Correct meaning of IP address

questions.subject: Computer Science
questions.text:
A. Write and call a Python function CopyShort() that reads the text file "Story.txt" and writes into a new text file "Brief.txt" only those lines that have fewer than 5 words.
For example, if "Story.txt" contains:
Once upon a time
there lived a clever fox in a forest near a river
It was hungry
It saw some grapes
then "Brief.txt" should contain:
Once upon a time
It was hungry
It saw some grapes
questions.model:
def CopyShort():
    fin = open("Story.txt", "r")
    fout = open("Brief.txt", "w")
    for line in fin:
        if len(line.split()) < 5:
            fout.write(line)
    fin.close()
    fout.close()

CopyShort()

points.t: Correct function header
Opening Story.txt in read mode and Brief.txt in write mode
Correct logic: counting the words of each line with split() and writing lines with fewer than 5 words
Correctly calling the function

or.text:
B. Write a Python function LongestWord() that reads the text file "Quote.txt" and displays the longest word in the file along with its length. (If two words are equally long, display the one that comes first.)
For example, if the file contains:
Knowledge grows when shared
Practice makes progress
the function should display:
Knowledge 9
or.model:
def LongestWord():
    f = open("Quote.txt", "r")
    words = f.read().split()
    f.close()
    longest = ""
    for w in words:
        if len(w) > len(longest):
            longest = w
    print(longest, len(longest))

points.t: Correct function header
Opening and reading the file, splitting into words
Correct logic to find the longest word
Displaying the word and its length

questions.subject: Computer Science
questions.text: A web browser stores the names of the pages visited in a stack named History (implemented as a list). Write the following user-defined functions in Python:

parts.q:
I. visit(stack, page): push page onto the stack, but only if it is not the same as the page at the top of the stack (so that reloading a page does not store it twice).
For example, after visit(History, "Home"), visit(History, "News"), visit(History, "News"), visit(History, "Sports") and visit(History, "Scores"), History should be ['Home', 'News', 'Sports', 'Scores'].
parts.model:
def visit(stack, page):
    if stack == [] or stack[-1] != page:
        stack.append(page)

points.t: Correct condition: the stack is empty or its top element stack[-1] is not the same as page
Pushing page using append()

parts.q:
II. back(stack, n): pop n pages from the stack (or fewer, if the stack becomes empty), displaying each page as it is popped, and then return the page now at the top of the stack, or "Empty" if no page is left.
For the stack above, back(History, 2) should display Scores and Sports (one per line) and return "News".
parts.model:
def back(stack, n):
    count = 0
    while stack != [] and count < n:
        print(stack.pop())
        count += 1
    if stack == []:
        return "Empty"
    return stack[-1]

points.t: Correct loop that pops at most n pages and stops if the stack becomes empty
Correct pop() and display of each page
Returning the top page stack[-1], or "Empty" when the stack is empty

or.text: B. Write a Python function split_marks(D) that takes a dictionary D whose keys are student names and values are marks (out of 100). The function should return two lists: the names of students who scored 33 or more, and the names of those who scored less than 33. Also write statements to call it for {"Asha": 72, "Bilal": 28, "Charu": 33, "Dev": 15} and display both lists.
or.model:
def split_marks(D):
    passed = []
    failed = []
    for name in D:
        if D[name] >= 33:
            passed.append(name)
        else:
            failed.append(name)
    return passed, failed

marks = {"Asha": 72, "Bilal": 28,
         "Charu": 33, "Dev": 15}
p, f = split_marks(marks)
print(p, f)
Output: ['Asha', 'Charu'] ['Bilal', 'Dev']

points.t: Correct function header
Correct loop over the dictionary with the condition
Returning both lists
Correct call and display of both lists

questions.text: Mrs. Fernandes, a class teacher, wants to keep the marks of her students in a CSV file named Marks.csv. The first row of the file is the header row RollNo, Name, Maths, Science, and each following row is the record of one student. Write the following user-defined functions:

import csv
def create_file():
    data = [[1, "Aman", 78, 82], [2, "Bela", 65, 70],
            [3, "Chirag", 90, 88], [4, "Divya", 72, 79]]
    f = open("Marks.csv", "w", newline="")

import csv
def toppers():
    f = open("Marks.csv", "r")
    r = csv.reader(f)

import pickle
def AddPlayer():

parts.q: II. Bonus(): increase the Points of every player whose Sport is "Chess" by 10, and save the changes in Players.dat.
parts.model:
import pickle
def Bonus():
    records = []
    f = open("Players.dat", "rb")
    try:
        while True:
            rec = pickle.load(f)
            if rec["Sport"] == "Chess":
                rec["Points"] = rec["Points"] + 10
            records.append(rec)
    except EOFError:
        f.close()
    f = open("Players.dat", "wb")
    for rec in records:
        pickle.dump(rec, f)
    f.close()
Note: import pickle may be written once for the whole program. (Updating in place using rb+ mode with seek() is also correct.)

points.t: Correct function header and opening the file in rb mode
Using pickle.load() in a loop with try-except EOFError
Checking Sport and increasing Points by 10
Writing all the records back to the file (wb mode with dump())

questions.subject: Computer Science
questions.text:
Pragati Textiles is setting up a new factory unit in Surat. Its head office is in Kolkata. The Surat unit has four buildings: DESIGN, PRODUCTION, STORE and OFFICE. As a network expert, suggest the best solutions for the questions (I) to (V), keeping in mind the distances and other details given below.
Distance between the buildings:
FromToDistance
DESIGNPRODUCTION120 m
DESIGNSTORE60 m
DESIGNOFFICE50 m
PRODUCTIONSTORE70 m
PRODUCTIONOFFICE140 m
STOREOFFICE80 m
Number of computers in each building:
BuildingComputers
DESIGN80
PRODUCTION35
STORE15
OFFICE40

parts.q: I. Suggest the most suitable building to install the server, with a suitable reason.
parts.model: DESIGN, because it has the maximum number of computers (80).

points.t: DESIGN with the reason: maximum number of computers

parts.q: II. Draw the cable layout to connect all the buildings using star topology, with the server building at the centre.
parts.model: Star layout with DESIGN at the centre: DESIGN to PRODUCTION (120 m), DESIGN to STORE (60 m) and DESIGN to OFFICE (50 m). The drawing shows three cables going out from DESIGN.

points.t: Star layout with DESIGN at the centre connected to PRODUCTION, STORE and OFFICE (drawn or described)

parts.q:
III. Suggest the placement of the following devices in the layout of part II, with justification:
a. Repeater
b. Switch
parts.model:
a. A repeater should be placed on the cable between DESIGN and PRODUCTION, because this cable is 120 m long, which is more than 100 m.
b. A switch should be placed in every building, to connect the computers of that building.

points.t: a. Repeater between DESIGN and PRODUCTION (distance more than 100 m)
b. Switch in every building

parts.q: IV. The STORE building is next to a power generator that causes a lot of electrical interference. Which wired medium should be used for the DESIGN to STORE link so that the signal is not affected by this interference? Give one more advantage of this medium.
parts.model: Optical fibre cable: it carries data as light, so electromagnetic noise cannot affect it. One more advantage: it has a higher bandwidth, so the data transfer rate is higher (signals can also travel longer distances).

points.t: Optical fibre cable
Any one more advantage: higher bandwidth / higher data transfer rate / signals travel longer distances

parts.q: V. A. The design team has to send large design files to the head office in Kolkata. Which protocol is meant for transferring files from one computer to another?

points.t: FTP (File Transfer Protocol)

or.q: V. B. The head office in Kolkata sends daily production reports to the Surat unit by e-mail. Expand SMTP and state what it is used for.
or.model: SMTP: Simple Mail Transfer Protocol. It is the protocol used for e-mail services, that is, for sending e-mail messages.

points.t: SMTP: Simple Mail Transfer Protocol
Use: sending e-mail (e-mail services)
